data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra that has raised $11.5M to date. The Climate & Energy sector includes one public comparable (Linz AG, LNZA) and eight private peers, though the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with comparable valuations to support a traditional peer-median approach.

Given the scarcity of narrow-filter peers in this segment, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $12M raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $29M. This method assumes Karman will meet standard milestones warranting the step-up before Series A fundraising.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M to $33M, with $29M as the median point. Key uncertainties include the company's progress toward product-market fit, capital efficiency relative to climate-tech cohort norms, and whether the sector's public and private comparables accurately reflect Karman's risk profile and growth trajectory. The single-method triangulation—necessitated by peer-set constraints—carries elevated sensitivity to the 2.5x multiplier assumption; tighter calibration would require either narrower climate-tech seed comps or visibility into Series A market conditions for similar companies.
